questions.question: How much notice does the Brightwater supply agreement require to terminate for convenience?
questions.raw_output: The agreement itself requires ninety days: 8.1 Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience by giving ninety (90) days' written notice to the other. The First Amendment did not change this, stating that the Agreement continues in full force and effect, including the Unit Price, the Minimum Annual Volume, the Liability Cap and the notice period for termination for convenience. However, the quick-reference memo conflicts with this, stating that either party must give sixty (60) days' written notice. Because of this conflict, the memo's sixty-day figure should be checked against the agreement before anyone relies on it.

questions.question: What uptime has Orion committed to, per the contract documents?
questions.raw_output: The documents conflict on Orion's uptime commitment. The Pricing Schedule states that Orion's committed Platform uptime is 99.5% per calendar month, excluding scheduled maintenance. The Service Level Agreement states that Orion commits to a monthly Platform availability of 99.9%, measured across each calendar month at the Orion ingest gateway and excluding Scheduled Maintenance. Both documents are marked as in force, and none of the provided excerpts says which one prevails.

questions.question: How long do we have to keep contractor invoices and maintenance work orders?
questions.raw_output: The documents conflict on this. The Operations Memo says maintenance work orders, contractor invoices and callout sheets held by the operations department shall be kept for five (5) years from the end of the fiscal year in which they were closed, and may then be deleted from the shared drive by the stations supervisor. The Records Retention Policy says financial records, including general ledgers, payment vouchers, supplier invoices, contractor invoices and maintenance work orders, shall be retained for seven (7) years from the end of the fiscal year in which they were created, and it applies to every employee, contractor and board member who creates or receives records on behalf of the Authority. Both documents are marked as in force (the memo is effective 2024-08-12 and the policy 2025-07-01), and neither says which one prevails, so this conflict should be resolved by whoever owns these documents before any deletion happens.
